correlation_analysis.analysis_summary: No log events were provided for analysis, therefore no direct event-to-technique mappings could be created. Retrieval of relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques succeeded, and the focus remains on preparing detection and response controls for the identified techniques.
overall_recommendations: Implement baseline monitoring for the following high‑relevance techniques: Valid Accounts (T1078), Account Discovery (T1087), Remote Services (T1021), PowerShell (T1086), Windows Management Instrumentation (T1047), Permission Groups Discovery (T1069), Process Discovery (T1057), System Network Configuration Discovery (T1016), Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols (T1071.001), and Socket Filters (T1205.002).

Deploy and tune detection rules for Windows security events (e.g., 4624, 4627, 4672), Sysmon events (Process Creation, Process Access), and Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) events (5156/5158) to surface the behaviors described in the retrieved techniques.

Establish alert thresholds for anomalous activity such as logons from privileged or service accounts at unusual times or locations, unexpected PowerShell command lines (especially encoded payloads), non‑svchost processes invoking WMI, and outbound HTTP traffic to IPs outside the Azure metadata service range.

Create response playbooks that include credential verification, account lockout, lateral movement containment, and forensic collection of process trees and network connections when any of the above techniques are detected.
Regularly review and update the detection logic to reflect changes in the environment and emerging ATT&CK techniques beyond the current set.
